verdict.rationale: Elastic says it is built on OpenTelemetry from the ground up, ingests OTel and Prometheus remote-write data natively, and ships EDOT distributions it describes as having no vendor lock-in. That directly addresses instrumenting once with open standards and keeping backend portability. The evidence is mostly overview and marketing claims, though, and it also points to proprietary Elastic APM agents. Missing for 10: detailed docs showing EDOT stays upstream-compatible so backends can be swapped without code changes, feature parity for OTel-instrumented data versus Elastic APM agents, and independent or hands-on confirmation of backend switching.

support.subject: As an SRE, I can instrument once with open standards and switch backends without re-instrumenting my code

citations.quote: Elastic Distributions of OpenTelemetry (EDOT) delivers production-ready collection with no vendor lock-in.
Elastic is open by design, schema-agnostic, Prometheus-native, and built on OpenTelemetry (OTel) from the ground up.
Ingest metrics from any source using OpenTelemetry, Prometheus remote write, or Elastic Agent integrations.
